message.content:
**Answer** One of the most celebrated and widely recognized sculptures of the 19th century is **“The Kiss” (Le Baiser) by Auguste Rodin (1889)**. It has become an icon of Romanticism and modern sculpture, and it is still reproduced, displayed, and studied worldwide. --- ### Why “The Kiss” stands out | Feature | Details | |---------|---------| | **Artist** | Auguste Rodin (1840‑1917) – a pioneer of modern sculpture. | | **Date** | 1889 (first cast). | | **Style** | Romantic realism with a hint of Symbolism; it captures an intimate, almost erotic moment. | | **Material** | Bronze (originally cast in bronze; also marble versions). | | **Location** | Original bronze casts are housed in major museums (e.g., Musée Rodin in Paris, the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York). | | **Cultural Impact** | • Frequently reproduced in prints, postcards, and popular media.
• Influenced countless artists and became a symbol of love and passion.
• Its dramatic pose and emotional intensity made it a staple in art education. | --- ### Other 19th‑century sculptures that rival its fame | Sculpture | Artist | Year | Notable Features | |-----------|--------|------|------------------| | **The Statue of Liberty** | Frédéric Baron Houdon (design), Alexandre Garnier‑Sicard (sculpture) | 1886 | A monumental allegorical figure representing liberty; a national symbol of the United States. | | **The Gates of Hell** | Auguste Rodin | 1880‑1917 | A massive bronze relief inspired by Dante’s *Inferno*; a monumental work that influenced modern sculpture. | | **The Thinker** | Auguste Rodin | 1902‑03 (early 20th century) | Though technically post‑19th, it was conceived in the late 19th and remains one of Rodin’s most iconic works. | | **The Venus de Milo** | (Ancient) | 150 BC (but rediscovered in 1820) | Rediscovery in the 19th century sparked renewed interest in classical sculpture. | --- ### Bottom line While several 19th‑century sculptures have left a lasting legacy, **“The Kiss” by Rodin** is often cited as the most famous due to its widespread reproduction, influence on modern art, and enduring presence in popular culture.
